description: The objective of the Rodent Research-10 mission (RR-10) was to investigate how spaceflight affects the cellular and molecular mechanisms of normal bone tissue regeneration in space. To this end, ten (10) 14-15 weeks-old female B6129SF2/J Wild Type (WT), and ten (10) 14-15 weeks-old female B6;129S2-Cdkn1atm1Tyj/J (p21-null) mice received a pre-flight subcutaneous injection of the bone marker (Alizarin Red), and were then delivered to the ISS aboard SpaceX-21. At 7 days before euthanasia, all 20 mice received an intraperitoneal (IP) injection with a bone formation marker (Calcein). At 48 +/- 2 hours before euthanasia, all 20 mice received an IP injection with a second dose of Calcein as well as a cell proliferation marker (BrdU). Then, following 28-29 days in microgravity, the Flight mice were euthanized. Following removal of hindlimbs, carcasses were wrapped in aluminum foil, preserved in the CryoChiller, and stored at -80 C or colder until return to Earth. In addition to the Flight group, three ground control groups were also part of the study: Basal (representing the pre-launch state), Vivarium (standard vivarium housing for the same duration of time as flight), and Ground (flight habitat in the International Space Station Environment Simulator, ISSES). Twenty mice (10 of each strain) were included in each of these control groups (except Vivarium which included 12 of each strain). These were treated, euthanized and processed on the same schedule and in the same manner as the flight samples. This study includes bulk RNA sequencing ribodepleted gene expression data from the cecum of 20 Basal animals (10 WT and 10 p21-null), 10 Flight animals (5 WT and 5 p21-null), 10 Ground animals (5 WT and 5 p21-null), and 24 Vivarium animals (12 WT and 12 p21-null).
funding: The sequencing analysis was funded by the NASA Space Biology program within the NASA Science Mission Directorate's (SMD) Biological and Physical Sciences (BPS) Division.

payloads.description:
Rodent Research-10 (RR-10) investigates the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying bone regenerative deficits due to disuse on Earth and microgravity in space. This mission examined how aging influences the regenerative potential of the femoral bone marrow stem cell populations.  Specifically, the study examined the role of a gene – Cdkn1a – that produces the CDKN1A protein – that inhibits cell cycle progression in cells. RR-10 (20 female mice, 13-17 weeks old, B6129SF2/J Wild Type (WT) and B6;129S2-Cdkn1atm1Tyj/J (p21-null) to assess the CDKN1a/p21 pathway in regenerative bone formation. The mice will be maintained on the ISS for ~30 days.  This mission was sponsored by NASA.

Tissue degeneration and the failure of tissue to regenerate normally in microgravity are increasing concerns for sustaining life in space, as the duration of future flight missions increase. The cellular mechanisms activated by microgravity unloading in mouse bone during spaceflight are not completely understood, but they include inhibition of the differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells and activation of the CDKN1a/p21-mediated cell cycle arrest in proliferative osteoprecursor cells on the bone surface.

In addition to the Flight group, three ground control groups were also part of the study: Basal (representing the pre-launch state), Vivarium (standard vivarium housing for the same duration of time as flight), and Ground (flight habitat in the International Space Station Environment Simulator, ISSES). Twenty mice (10 of each strain) were included in each of these control groups (except Vivarium which included 12 of each strain). These were treated, euthanized and processed on the same schedule and in the same manner as the flight samples. This study includes spatially resolved transcriptional profiling data from hippocampi from 5 WT flight animals, and 5 WT ground control animals. Hippocampi from the right hemisphere were embedded and cryosectioned. Cryosections were placed on gene expression arrays, stained and imaged. Imaging was followed by tissue permeabilization to release mRNA molecules from cells for capture onto the array surface. Subsequently, spatial transcriptomics libraries were prepared and sequenced.

PI: Eduardo Almeida, Ph.D.
Co-Investigators: Elizabeth Blaber, Ph.D., Ruth Globus, Ph.D., Yasaman Shirazi-Fard, Ph.D., Cassandra Juran, Ph.D.

The mission objectives

To test, in vivo, the hypothesis that CDKN1a/p21 is the key effector of cell cycle arrest in bone tissue in response to the stresses of spaceflight, the following specific aims of the Role of CDKN1a/p21 Pathway in Microgravity-Induced Bone Tissue Regenerative Arrest – A Spaceflight Study of Transgenic CDKN1a/p21-Null Mice in Microgravity (Rodent Research-10) investigation are addressed:

•	Determine and compare the extent of osteoblast proliferation, differentiation, and mineral deposition in microgravity and in 1g (Earth gravity equivalent) in a CDKN1a/p21-null mutant versus wild type (WT) mice.
•	Assess whether the coupling and balance of increased osteoclastogenesis and decreased osteoblastogenesis in microgravity is altered in a CDKN1a/p21-null background.
•	Determine whether CDKN1a/p21 expression in microgravity is regulated via mRNA stabilization by the microgravity-induced Cold Induced RNA Binding Protein (CIRBP) in response to oxidative stress in bone.

When completed, these studies will allow researchers to determine whether the presence of CDKN1a/p21 during mechanical unloading in microgravity induces arrest of bone growth and regeneration in vivo. The results from these studies also provide researchers with information to evaluate how CDKN1a/p21-mediated inhibition of osteoblast proliferation and differentiation may be coupled to osteoclastic activity induced by microgravity. Furthermore, these studies seek to connect the potential effector molecular mechanism of regenerative arrest in bone (by CDKN1a/p21) to its inducer, hypothesized here to be stabilization of CDKN1a/p21 message RNA by the oxidative (and other) stress response gene CIRBP.


IACUC Protocol Number:  RR-10

All animal procedures performed in these experiments were approved by the Institutional Animal Care and use Committees (IACUC) numbers NASA: RR-10 for flight at the NASA Ames Research Center (ARC) and the Kennedy Space Center (KSC) and the methods were carried out in accordance with relevant guidelines and regulations.

NASA Space Biology Biospecimen Sharing Program Activities 

The NASA Space Biology Biospecimen Sharing Program collected biospecimens from RR-10 to maximize the scientific return from the biological spaceflight.  The collected tissues included the following:  Duodenum., Jejunum, Pancreas, Stomach.


Available Data

The RR-10 payload produced the following Data (from checklist Excel file):

-	Animal enclosure temperature and relative humidity flight and ground data
-	Live Animal Return sensor accelerometer data 
-	ISS cabin and ground simulation chamber environmental monitoring data  
-	Rodent data including preflight data, operations time logs, sample shipment data.

protocols.name: Animal Husbandry

protocols.description: At the end of RR-10 experiment, all frozen carcasses and preserved hindlimbs were returned to the PI. In May 2021, the Biospecimen Sharing Program (BSP) team performed complex, integrated dissections at NASA Ames Research Center with the Principal Investigator team. Cecem tissues were kept at -80C freezer until processing. Baseline dissections were performed 7 days after launch following the same procedures used for the Flight animals.
protocols.name: sample collection

protocols.description: RNA was extracted using the AllPrep DNA/RNA Mini Kit (Qiagen, Valencia, CA) following GeneLab SOP 3.1-Qiagen AllPrep DNA/RNA Mini with Qiagen RNase-Free DNase set. Homogenization buffer for RNA purification was made by adding 1:100 beta-mercaptoethanol to Buffer RLT (Qiagen, Valencia, CA) and kept on ice until use. Approximately 20 mg of tissue was isolated using a scalpel, weighed, and immediately placed in 700 uL of the Buffer RLT solution. Homogenization was performed using tissue homogenizing bead mix red, (Next Advance, Raymertown, NY) on Bullet Blender Gold 24 (Next Advance, Raymertown, NY) for 3 minutes at 4 C per SOP 2.1-Tissue homogenization Using Bullet Blender Gold Bead Beater. Homogenates were centrifuged for 5 minutes at RT and 14,000 g to remove cell debris. The supernatant from each sample was then used to isolate and purify DNA and RNA following the manufacturer protocol. RNA was eluted in 35 uL RNAse free H2O, and DNA was eluted in 50 uL RNAse free H2O. Concentration for all RNA samples were measured using Qubit 3.0 Fluorometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA) with Qubit RNA BR kit following SOP 4.1-RNA/DNA/miRNA/cDNA Quantification using Qubit Fluorimeter. RNA quality was assessed using the Agilent 4200 TapeStation with the Agilent RNA ScreenTape (Agilent Technologies, Santa Clara, CA). DNA quality and size were assessed using the Agilent 4200 TapeStation with Agilent gDNA ScreenTape Kit (Agilent Technologies, Santa Clara, CA). GeneLab Sample Processing SOP can be found at the GitHub page, https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab-sampleProcessing/tree/master/SOP_docs
protocols.name: Nucleic Acid Extraction

protocols.description: ERCC ExFold RNA Spike-In Mixes (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA, Cat 4456739, v92), Mix 1 or Mix 2, were added on the day of library prep at the concentrations suggested by the manufacturer protocol. SOP 5.2 Use of ERCC Spike-In Mixes and UMRR/UHRR Controls for Total RNA Sequencing. GeneLab Sample Processing SOP can be found at the GitHub page, https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab-sampleProcessing/tree/master/SOP_docs.
protocols.name: Spike-in Protocol

protocols.description: RNA ribo depletion and library preparation was done with Illumina TruSeq Stranded Total RNA Library Prep Gold (Illumina Inc., San Diego, CA) following GeneLab SOP 5.1 Ilumina TruSeq Stranded Total RNA Lirary Prep using epMotion. Input RNA were approximately 500 ng with RIN greater than 4. Index adapters used were at 1.5 uM ( ILMN TruSeq RNA UD Indexes V2, lot 20958275). 15 cycles PCR were performed. Library fragment size was assessed using Agilent 4200 TapeStation with D1000 DNA ScreenTape (Agilent Technologies, Santa Clara, CA) following GeneLab SOP 6.3 Quality analysis of sequencing libraries using 4200 TapeStation System with D1000 reagent kit. Pooled library concentration was measured by Qubit 4 Fluorometer (ThermoFisher Scentific, Waltham, MA) following SOP 4.1-RNA/DNA/miRNA/cDNA Quantification using Qubit Fluorimeter. Library quality assessment was performed on iSeq100 (Illumina, San Diego, CA). GeneLab Sample Processing SOP can be found at the GitHub page, https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab-sampleProcessing/tree/master/SOP_docs.
protocols.name: Library Construction

protocols.description: RNA sequencing was performed by GeneLab Sample Processing Lab on Illumina NovaSeq 6000. Sequencing was set up as following: Read 1: 151 bp, Index1: 10 bp, Index2: 10 bp, Read 2: 151 bp. PhiX v3 was included as control and to increase library diversity. Protocol followed is SOP 7.1-Setting up NovaSeq 6000 and iSeq 100 Sequencers. GeneLab Sample Processing SOP can be found at the GitHub page, https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab-sampleProcessing/tree/master/SOP_docs.
protocols.name: Nucleic Acid Sequencing

protocols.description: Quality assessment of reads was performed with FastQC v0.12.1 and reports were combined with MultiQC v1.26. rRNA percentages of reads were estimated with the 'hts_SeqScreener' program of htstream v1.3.2 screened against a fasta file of M. musculus rRNA sequences retrieved from NCBI on 09-05-2025.
protocols.name: GeneLab raw data processing protocol

protocols.description: Data were processed as described in GL-DPPD-7101-G (https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab_Data_Processing/blob/master/RNAseq/Pipeline_GL-DPPD-7101_Versions/GL-DPPD-7101-G.md), using NF_RCP version 2.1.0 (https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab_RNASeq_Workflow/tree/NF_RCP_2.1.0). In short, raw fastq files were filtered using Trim Galore! (version 0.6.10) powered by Cutadapt (version 4.2). Trimmed fastq file quality was evaluated with FastQC (version 0.12.1), and MultiQC (version 1.26) was used to generate MultiQC reports. Mus Musculus STAR and RSEM references were built using STAR (version 2.7.11b) and RSEM (version 1.3.3), respectively, Ensembl release 112, genome assembly GRCm39 (Mus_musculus.GRCm39.dna.primary_assembly.fa) concatenated with ERCC92.fa from ThermoFisher (https://assets.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/ERCC92.zip), and the following gtf annotation file: Mus_musculus.GRCm39.112.gtf concatenated with the ERCC92.gtf file from ThermoFisher (https://assets.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/ERCC92.zip). Trimmed reads were aligned to the Mus Musculus + ERCC STAR reference with STAR (version 2.7.11b) and alignment log files were compiled with MultiQC (version 1.26). Aligned reads were assessed for strandedness using RSeQC infer_experiment.py (version 5.0.4), gene body coverage using RSeQC geneBody_coverage.py (version 5.0.4), inner distance was assessed using RSeQC inner_distance.py (version 5.0.4), and distribution of RNA features using RSeQC read_distribution.py (version 5.0.4). Aligned reads from all samples were quantified using RSEM (version 1.3.3), with strandedness set to reverse and RSEM count log files were compiled with MultiQC (version 1.26). A runsheet was generated with dp_tools (version 1.3.8) and the runsheet and quantification data were imported to R (version 4.4.2) with tximport (version 1.34.0) to generate the RSEM raw counts data. A set of rRNA-removed raw counts data was also created by removing Ensembl IDs that map to ribosomal RNA (rRNA) from the RSEM gene count data. Assessment of ERCC spiked genes was performed as detailed in the ERCC_analysis_GLbulkRNAseq.html report.
protocols.name: GeneLab RNAseq data processing protocol
